observation.visible_scene: A bonfire made of a low pile of dry sticks and branches burns in the foreground on bare ground. Behind it lies a flat green crop field, a cluster of palm trees on the right, and on the left distant hills, a few small buildings, and a low sun setting into orange-pink clouds. The framing is fixed; the horizon, palms, buildings and stick pile stay in the same positions throughout.
visible_changes: The flames continuously flicker and deform in place: the bright yellow core at the base pulses in size and brightness, and orange flame tongues rise, thin out, lean left or right, and re-form.

The overall height and silhouette of the flame column vary frame to frame (e.g., taller and more vertical around t=0.13, 0.67, 1.07, 1.60, 1.87, 2.00; lower and more spread around t=0.27, 0.40, 0.80, 1.20, 1.40, 2.27), but the fire does not translate as a whole.

A straight horizontal seam runs across the upper part of the flame in most frames; below it the fire is sharp and detailed, above it the orange glow is softer and more diffuse, behaving like a separate composited layer rather than natural flame.
The stacked sticks, the ground, the field, the palms and the sunset sky show no motion; the camera does not pan, tilt or zoom.
Sparks/embers occasionally appear detached to the right of the flame (e.g., t=0.00, 0.60, 1.20, 1.60) and vanish in adjacent frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the fire and whether it intensifies or dies out after this excerpt.
The true shape of the flame above the horizontal seam if that seam is a compositing/loop boundary.
The full duration of the source video and any events before t=0 or after t=2.67.
uncertain_details: Whether the horizontal line at the top of the flame is an editing/compositing seam or a physical edge of the scene; the soft glow above it could be smoke, a separate overlay, or a loop artifact.
Whether the detached orange specks are airborne embers or compositing noise.
